activity_context.topic_title: Solving Quadratic Inequalities Using the Graphical Method

feedback.problem:
Solve the inequality $6{x}^{2}+21x\ge 12$ and express the solution set in interval notation.

$x\in (${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$]\,⋃\,[${{field-3}}$,\,\infty )$
feedback.worked_solution:
To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the terms to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}+21x & \ge 12 \\ 6{x}^{2}+21x-12 & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y=6{x}^{2}+21x-12$ lies **above** the $x$-axis or touches this axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}+21x-12 & =0 \\ (6{x}^{2}-3x)+(24x-12) & =0 \\ 3x(2x-1)+12(2x-1) & =0 \\ (3x+12)(2x-1) & =0 \\ 3(x+4)(2x-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=-4$ and $x=\frac{1}{2},$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14059052/assets/38c1897ec93625527b48ec689fbd65e9a63056e033fa6a7a0c72473f1188e7ea.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
6{x}^{2}+21x-12\ge 0,
$$

 

we look for the part of the parabola that is **above** the $x$-axis or touches this axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\le -4$ or $x\ge \frac{1}{2}.$

Using interval notation, we write $x\in (-\infty ,-4]⋃[\frac{1}{2},\infty ).$
